crates/domain/src/mutation.rs (MutationError: 12 variants) mirrored as a local snake_case `Reason` schemars enum in crates/mcp-server/src/stdio/mutation.rs:209-226, used by the 5 M2 mutation tools (rust.manifest.patch, rust.fmt.apply, rust.fix.apply, rust.dependency.add, rust.dependency.remove); rust.analyzer.action.apply also maps MutationError internally (crates/mcp-server/src/stdio/mutation/analyzer_action.rs:808-820) but wires it onto its own SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE `ApplyCode` enum (crates/mcp-server/src/stdio/mutation/analyzer_action.rs:171-205, 30 variants) rather than exposing the snake_case Reason on the wire

code_casing_by_family.mutation_tools (5): snake_case (e.g. invalid_operation, permission_denied); rust.manifest.patch, rust.fmt.apply, rust.fix.apply, rust.dependency.add, rust.dependency.remove only (see findings[] F11)

error_codes_enum_by_tool.rust.project.open: BlockedCode (7 variants) + UnavailableCode (2 variants), crates/mcp-server/tests/snapshots/project-open-tool.json $defs; error_codes[] lists both enums merged and sorted
error_codes_enum_by_tool.rust.analyzer.action.apply: ApplyCode (30 variants), crates/mcp-server/tests/snapshots/analyzer-action-apply-tool.json $defs; SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE, not the M2 snake_case Reason (see findings[] F11)

inconsistencies: Two different closed-enum casing conventions coexist for the same conceptual field (`error_code`): SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE for the 31 read/analysis tools' OperationalErrorCode-derived codes, snake_case for the 5 M2 mutation tools' Reason codes. An agent or generic client cannot assume one casing convention across the whole 36-tool catalog. See findings[] F5, F11.

The base OperationalErrorCode (9 variants) is extended per-tool with additional tool-specific SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE variants inside each tool's own schemars-derived Code enum (e.g. audit adds nine AUDIT_* variants, quality.gate adds two QUALITY_GATE_* variants); there is no single shared closed enum across all 31 read/analysis tools, only a shared naming convention and a shared 9-variant floor. This is architecturally consistent with 'no ampliar enums compartidos silenciosamente' (roadmap G1) but means error_codes[] must be read per-tool, never assumed global.

findings.evidence: The 31 read/analysis tools serialize `error_code` using `OperationalErrorCode`-derived enums with `#[serde(rename_all = "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE")]` (e.g. PROJECT_NOT_FOUND); this includes `rust.analyzer.action.apply`, whose closed error enum is `ApplyCode` (30 variants, SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE), not the M2 Reason mirror. The 5 M2 mutation tools (manifest.patch, fmt.apply, fix.apply, dependency.add, dependency.remove) serialize their local `Reason` mirror of `MutationError` (crates/domain/src/mutation.rs:113-124) with `#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]` (e.g. invalid_operation). Both are closed contracts (deny_unknown_fields-equivalent enum sets) but use incompatible casing conventions for the same conceptual field. Corrected per audit R01 finding F11 (docs/validation/M8/delegation/R01-census-traceability/report.md §3): an earlier version of this finding and 01-census.md §6 incorrectly counted `rust.analyzer.action.apply` among the snake_case tools.
findings.proposed_fix: Before the 0.8 freeze (D11/ADR-012), decide and document explicitly whether this dual casing is intentional (mutation tools use a distinct envelope by design, per ADR-050..058) or should be unified; either way, state it in docs/compatibility.md so client authors do not assume one casing pattern catalog-wide.

findings.evidence: The server declares the MCP resources capability and implements `read_resource`, but never overrides `list_resources`; there is no `list_resources`/`ListResourcesResult` handler anywhere under crates/mcp-server/src (grep confirmed no matches), so `resources/list` always returns `[]` regardless of session state. The only two Resource URI families that exist (`rust-artifact://…`, `rust-quality-artifact://…`) are ephemeral references minted inline inside tool call responses; a client can only discover a Resource URI by first calling a tool that returns one. The spec's own conceptual examples in §9.2 (`rust-project://workspace/metadata`, `rust-catalog://status`, `rust-catalog://crate/{name}`) were never implemented; ADR-011 explicitly left them optional for M1 ('si aporta valor') and they stayed unimplemented through M6.
findings.proposed_fix: No code defect — this is a deliberate, ADR-scoped design (dynamic, non-enumerable Resources). Recommend docs/tools.md and docs/compatibility.md state explicitly that Resources are non-enumerable and must be obtained from a prior tool response, so client authors do not rely on `resources/list` returning entries.

findings.evidence: The M2 mutation journal/receipt store has no in-file `format_version`/`schema_version` field (grep for format_version/schema_version/MAGIC across the 2949-line file returned no matches); its only version marker is the `-v1` suffix on the state-root subdirectory name (`rust-mcp-mutations-v1`, crates/mcp-server/src/host_config.rs:285). By contrast every other disk_formats[] entry in this census (catalog SQLite, catalog trust bundle, LanceDB index, security policy, quality-artifact payloads) carries an explicit field-level version marker.
findings.proposed_fix: For D12/M8-03, decide whether directory-name namespacing is sufficient for the mutation journal's migration story or whether an in-record format_version field should be added before 0.8 freeze; document the decision in the D12 brief.

findings.evidence: Common envelope $defs are redefined independently inside every tool's own inputSchema/outputSchema rather than shared once across the tools/list response: e.g. `Data` appears in 31/36 schemas, `Code` in 26/36, `Freshness` in 21/36, `Truncation` in 19/36, `RuntimeIdentity` in 16/36, `Provenance` in 14/36 (measured via target/m8-census/measure_details2.py-style $defs key count over crates/mcp-server/tests/snapshots/*.json). This is inherent to per-tool JSON Schema documents in MCP's `tools/list` (no cross-tool $ref is possible), not a bug, but it is the largest structural contributor to the 392,529-byte `tools/list` response the M8-01 gate of superficie must justify per spec §78/§85.
findings.proposed_fix: No code change recommended (protocol-level constraint); cite this measurement explicitly in the surface-gate context-cost discussion so 'large tools/list' is attributed to duplicated envelope shapes rather than genuinely tool-specific schema growth.
